content:
sanjay: quick sync — ran full profiling pass after the kernel-scheduler change landed. noticed model-specific regressions, sharing quick notes and suggested mitigations.

emma: thanks. high-level numbers?

sanjay: short summary: Mixtral-8B throughput dropped ~30% at common config (batch=4, seq=1024) — 135 tok/s -> 92 tok/s. Llama-13B p50 latency up ~12% for seq<=512. Qwen-7B got a small uplift (~8%) due to switching to rabit-matmul kernel.

li: ouch. any idea root cause for mixtral?

sanjay: kernel scheduler started preferring the new fused-attn path for many shapes. fused-attn is faster for long sequences but it forces a different KV layout and triggers an extra memcpy during KV cache warm-up for Mixtral's custom head dims. net effect: higher per-token cost for typical mixtral workloads which are short (avg ctx 256).

rachel: so workload mismatch between heuristics and observed context distribution. can we make scheduler shape-aware per-model?

sanjay: yes — we should. quick mitigation: add a per-model override to prefer the 'small-kernel' path when median(ctx_len) < 512 or when model kv_dim != expected. implemented a test patch locally:

sanjay: ```
model_tuning:
  Mixtral-8B:
    kernel_preference: small
    batching_heuristic:
      short_context_threshold: 384
      prefer_continuous_kv: false
```

emma: what's the KV-cache behavior note? you mentioned memcpy penalty.

sanjay: right — the fused path changes KV layout from [heads, kv_dim] contiguous to an interleaved layout. our runtime currently does a layout transform when reading/writing KV for every request if the model preference flips during rollouts. this shows up as ~0.7-1.2ms extra per-token for batched short requests.

li: can we cache transformed KV per-request-id to avoid repeated memcopies?

sanjay: possible, but memory ballooning is a concern for Dedicated pools. cheaper fix: make kernel selection stable per-worker per-model version and avoid switching mid-stream. also add a small LRU per-worker cache keyed by (model_ver, layout) for transformed KV pages. low mem budget (64MB) should still help hit common cases.

rachel: what about batching heuristics? any tuning there?

sanjay: yes. observed that continuous batching helps long-seq throughput but penalizes short ctx p50 latency. new heuristic proposal:

sanjay: ```
batching:
  max_batch_items: 8
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
  enable_continuous_batching: auto
  continuous_batching_threshold: 256  # only turn on if median ctx > 256
  prefer_small_kernels_for_short_ctx: true
```

emma: did you run throughputs across batch sizes?

sanjay: run summary (seq=256 unless noted):
- Mixtral-8B: batch1=48 tok/s, batch2=85 tok/s, batch4=92 tok/s (regressed vs before change)
- Llama-13B: batch1=18 tok/s, batch2=34 tok/s, batch4=60 tok/s (p50 up ~12%)
- Qwen-7B: batch1=62 tok/s, batch2=118 tok/s, batch4=210 tok/s (improved)

perf-bot: perf report attached: 
```
perf-bot: MODEL Mixtral-8B | seq=256 | batch=4 | tokens/s=92 | p50=18.6ms | p95=42.1ms | kv_memcpy_ms_per_token=0.95
perf-bot: MODEL Llama-13B  | seq=512 | batch=2 | tokens/s=60 | p50=24.4ms | p95=78.9ms | kv_memcpy_ms_per_token=0.12
perf-bot: MODEL Qwen-7B    | seq=1024| batch=4 | tokens/s=210| p50=12.2ms | p95=28.7ms | kv_memcpy_ms_per_token=0.05
```

li: kv_memcpy_ms_per_token correlates strongly with the regressions. We should surface a metric: kv_miss_rate or kv_layout_flip_count in the console.

sanjay: agreed. action items I propose:
- revert aggressive fused-kernel preference globally, add per-model kernel_preference override (short-term)
- add per-worker stable kernel pinning for active model versions
- add small per-worker transformed-KV LRU (64MB) behind flag for Dedicated
- add metrics: kv_layout_flip_count, kv_memcpy_ms_per_token, continuous_batching_on_ratio
- update optimizer suggestions in Redwood Optimize: prefer small-kernel profile for Mixtral where median(ctx)<384

rachel: timeline?

sanjay: I'll open a PR with the kernel_preference override and the metrics today (ETA EOD). li — can you prototype the LRU KV cache and measure memory/latency tradeoffs?

li: yep, will spike tomorrow and post numbers.

emma: nice. also add a small note in release docs about potential per-model regressions after kernel changes and how to opt-out.

perf-bot: regtests queued: run/1759001290 — will report back with full sweep CSV.

sanjay: thanks all. once PR merges we'll run the full continuous sweep across regions and feed results into the model catalog so Optimize can recommend settings automatically.

rachel: :thumbsup:
